newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA COURT SUSPENDS C.BANK LICENCE LIFTING.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA COURT SUSPENDS C.BANK LICENCE LIFTING.

text.p: A court in the central Romanian city of Cluj has suspended a central bank order withdrawing the operating licence of private bank Dacia Felix, court officials said on Thursday.
The president of the Cluj Court of Appeals said the court had halted the order until May 21 under legal proceedings launched by Dacia Felix against the central bank (BNR).
"The withdrawal of Dacia Felix's licence can only be enacted after the court rules on this case," court president Teodor Petrus said by telephone.
Dacia Felix challenged the legality of the BNR's order this week, saying it contradicted existing laws. Central bank officials were not immediately available for comment.
On Monday, the central bank stripped private banks Dacia Felix and Credit Bank of their authorisations after a deterioration of their financial position, paving the way for their liquidation.
Dacia Felix has been awaiting a decision by another Cluj court on its fate after the central bank lodged a case asking legal authorities to decide on liquidation or reorganisation.
A recovery plan drawn up by the bank provides for foreign capital injection, which must be approved by the central bank.
